headline: LOTUS RESOURCES SELLS 173K LBS OFF-SPEC URANIUM AT DISCOUNT — KAYELEKERA MALAWI RESTART HITS QUALITY HURDLE
snippet: Lotus Resources (ASX: LOT) agreed to sell approximately 173,000 pounds of off-specification uranium from its restarted Kayelekera mine in Malawi at a discount to spot price, in a move that generates near-term cash flow but flags product quality challenges at the restart operation. Off-spec uranium falls short of the conversion standards required by most utilities; selling at a discount is a pragmatic solution to monetise existing inventory, but it underscores that consistent delivery of spec-grade product remains the key operational hurdle before Kayelekera fully participates in the uranium bull market.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q3 2026: URANIUM REVENUE +67.3% YTD AS 190K LBS U3O8 DELIVERED — MULTI-ASSET RAMP ON TRACK
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE: URG) reported Q3 2026 results showing uranium sales revenue up 67.3% year-to-date, with 190,000 pounds of U3O8 delivered to utilities under long-term contracts during the quarter. Management described the simultaneous ramp at both Lost Creek and Shirley Basin in Wyoming as on track — a rare operational feat for a junior uranium producer that demonstrates ISR execution capacity across two separate facilities, adding credibility to the company's multi-year production growth plans at a time when utilities are urgently seeking contracted non-Russian supply.

headline: UZBEKISTAN PLANS TO DOUBLE URANIUM OUTPUT TO 15,000 TONNES/YEAR BY 2030 — NAVOIYURAN EXPANDS CAPACITY
snippet: Uzbekistan's state uranium miner Navoiyuran is targeting production of 15,000 tonnes per year by 2030, up from approximately 7,500 tonnes currently, following a presidential briefing on the country's strategic mineral production plans. Uzbekistan is the world's seventh-largest uranium producer; a planned doubling of output would represent a meaningful addition to global supply at a time when uranium spot prices are near 19-year highs — investors pricing in sustained supply tightness should note that this timeline, if achieved, would bring significant new non-Russian, non-Kazakh pounds to market by the second half of this decade.

headline: RARE EARTH STOCKS TUMBLE — USAR -11% ON Q3 MISS, MP MATERIALS -5%, ENERGY FUELS -8% AS RATE-HIKE FEARS HIT SECTOR
snippet: Rare earth equities suffered broad declines on November 10 after a hotter-than-expected CPI print pushed December rate-hike odds above 80%, with USA Rare Earth (USAR) leading losses at -11% after Q3 adjusted loss widened to $0.44 per share — overshadowing the company's first commercial magnet sales milestone and the start of Serra Verde commercial-scale heavy rare earth shipments. MP Materials fell 5% despite Q3 NdPr production rising 41% year-over-year with a surprise adjusted profit, while Energy Fuels retreated 8% — a sector-wide repricing that illustrates how rising real interest rates disproportionately punish unprofitable or early-stage rare earth producers regardless of operational progress.

headline: MP MATERIALS Q3 EARNINGS BEAT: NdPr PRODUCTION +41% YoY, SALES VOLUME +94% — SURPRISE ADJUSTED PROFIT
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reported Q3 2026 results showing NdPr rare earth production up 41% year-over-year and sales volumes up 94%, delivering a surprise adjusted profit that bucked the sector trend. The result positions MP as the rare earth producer closest to standalone US profitability, with its Mountain Pass, California operation now scaling toward full commercial output — a critical data point for investors assessing which rare earth equities have the balance-sheet resilience to withstand the current rate-hike-driven selloff and emerge as long-term winners in the Western supply chain.

headline: AUSTRAL RESOURCES WINS 99.8% SHAREHOLDER VOTE FOR HAMMER METALS DEAL — COPPER SCHEME COURT HEARING NOV 13
snippet: Austral Resources' proposed acquisition of Hammer Metals cleared its shareholder hurdle with a 99.8% vote in favour at a scheme meeting, paving the way for a Second Court Hearing on November 13 and expected scheme implementation by November 25. The deal consolidates two copper-focused explorers with adjacent tenements in Queensland's Mount Isa region, combining Hammer's exploration pipeline with Austral's more advanced Mount Colin copper-cobalt project — a consolidation play that reflects the growing strategic logic of reducing per-ounce discovery costs in the same mineralised district rather than chasing greenfield ground.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES AFTER WORST WEEK SINCE MARCH — SHFE STOCKS COLLAPSE 24% TO 3-YEAR LOW OF 33,848 TONNES
snippet: Copper prices bounced on November 9 after their worst weekly decline since March, as Shanghai Futures Exchange-monitored warehouse stocks fell more than 24% in a week to 33,848 tonnes — the lowest level in nearly three years. The sharp drawdown in Chinese exchange inventories suggests physical demand is absorbing supply even as macro headwinds from US rate-hike expectations weigh on prices; ING analysts cautioned the bounce 'does not necessarily mark the end of the correction,' and with LME copper still down roughly 6% on the month, the tension between tight physical supply and weak macro sentiment defines copper's near-term setup.

headline: MARKET VOLATILITY BLOCKS CRITICAL MINERALS INVESTMENT — 25%+ OF ENERGY STORAGE DEVELOPERS SAY PRICE SWINGS HALT PROJECTS
snippet: A new DLA Piper report finds that price volatility is now cited by more than a quarter of energy storage developers, investors and mining companies as a primary barrier to critical minerals project investment — the highest share since the survey began. With lithium down over 20% in the past month and cobalt prices depressed, the report argues that commodity price swings function as a structural disincentive to long-term capital commitment, and suggests that government pricing backstops or offtake guarantees may be needed to unlock the billions in private capital required to build Western supply chains for battery metals, rare earths and other critical inputs.

headline: GOLD MINERS AT DECADE LOWS — 5.7X FORWARD EV/EBITDA VS. 9.9X IN 2014: VALUE TRAP OR CONTRARIAN ENTRY?
snippet: A new analysis finds gold producers trading near 5.7x forward EV/EBITDA — their lowest relative valuation since 2014's trough, when the industry was cutting dividends and writing down assets — against 9.9x multiples at prior peaks. The piece attributes the discount to three structural factors: operating leverage cuts both ways at high metal prices, capital return programmes remain nascent at most producers, and institutional coverage of junior names is thin. For self-directed retail investors deciding whether to add mining exposure on weakness at $4,000+ gold, the analysis offers a framework for distinguishing genuine value from a cyclical earnings peak masked by historically high metal prices.
